children.text: This video establishes a timeline of the humble origins of fan editing as a form of participatory culture. Early fan edits were primarily in small niche internet spaces that were shared by fans as a way to express their connection to media. The labor going into slicing and mixing the videos functioning as a celebratory act of the media. Understanding this history is important because it allows us to understand how current-day edits are circulated and contribute to an advertising-filled system.
where do we go from here

? Towards the conclusion the video gives several examples of the lines between fan edits functioning as a celebration to professional paid creators making advertisements is blurred especially on apps like Tiktok and Instagram where edits are everywhere getting over millions of views. There isn't anything wrong with creators being paid to make these videos, but it is such a far cry from the free labor of love editors used to engage in. It is just another example of art being sold and monetized. But it begs the question, do users on Tiktok know they are watching an ad? Are users aware of how much these short clips can influence our choices, because hiding behind these 6 second clips
are companies and business with a profit to earn not the fan girl.
